decisions.rationale: Farigiraf is the Trick Room setter and must be removed before it warps the game. Armor Tail blocks Fake Out and Bullet Punch, so the best line is double-targeting Farigiraf with Darkest Lariat + Mega Meteor Mash. Darkest Lariat does 60.8–113.8%; Mega Metagross Tough Claws Meteor Mash does ~44.7–84.0% (90% accurate). Minimum combined 105.5% guarantees the KO if both connect. If Farigiraf Protects, Trick Room stays off the field and we reset next turn. If Trick Room goes up as Farigiraf faints, the setter is gone and we play out 4 turns of room with Archaludon alone. Mega Evolving also ensures Metagross outspeeds Archaludon (143–178 vs 105–137).

reflections.summary: Lost the game and series mainly because the four brought could not consistently convert pressure into a win against the Rotom-Wash endgame. Archaludon eventually helped remove Dragapult and Metagross, while Mamoswine’s High Horsepower finished Metagross, but Rotom remained largely healthy and outlasted the weakened Archaludon. Draco Meteor misses into Incineroar and Dragapult cost substantial momentum, although there were no recorded decision errors and the late-game loss was not primarily a piloting mistake. The preview plan was mixed: Archaludon, Sinistcha, and Mamoswine all had useful roles, but Farigiraf was exposed to Metagross plus Incineroar pressure, and Mamoswine was a poor long-term answer to Rotom. No own Mega Stone holder was brought or evolved, so there was no Mega choice to evaluate. The registered six had relevant tools, but the supplied evidence does not establish that any of Altaria, Meowstic-Female, Qwilfish, or Dedenne was a materially better replacement; Armarouge and Sneasler were also untested, so the series loss cannot be attributed to a proven superior unused roster. There is insufficient evidence to judge whether between-game adjustments helped or backfired; in this game, the adjustment toward Sinistcha and Mamoswine produced useful progress but did not solve the matchup.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent, prioritize a reliable, accurate way to pressure or remove Rotom-Wash before committing Archaludon to an attrition endgame. Preserve the Rotom answer rather than using Mamoswine only as a Metagross check, and avoid relying on repeated Draco Meteor connections when a safer line is available. Farigiraf should not be left to absorb simultaneous Metagross and Incineroar pressure without stronger protection or immediate speed-control value. Re-evaluate the four from the full roster only if the unused Pokémon have verified tools against Rotom and Mega Metagross; no such advantage is demonstrated by the supplied data.
reflections.notebook: Observed opponent facts: Mega Metagross was Jolly and used Meteor Mash, Bullet Punch, Zen Headbutt, and Earthquake; it applies heavy physical pressure but can be threatened by strong Ground attacks. Incineroar revealed Intimidate, Fake Out, Darkest Lariat, Flare Blitz, and Parting Shot, with Sitrus Berry. Dragapult was Jolly Life Orb with Dragon Darts, Psychic Fangs, Will-O-Wisp, and U-turn; it can redirect pressure with burns and apply spread damage. Rotom-Wash was bulky with Leftovers, Levitate, Hydro Pump, Volt Switch, Will-O-Wisp, and Pain Split; it resisted Archaludon’s Flash Cannon and Thunderbolt, took only neutral Draco Meteor damage, healed through Pain Split, and was the decisive late-game obstacle. Preparation conclusion: bring a dependable Rotom answer and preserve it, while retaining an immediate answer to Mega Metagross. Do not build the plan around Archaludon repeatedly landing accurate Draco Meteors; its Stamina and special pressure are useful, but it struggles to finish a healthy Rotom. Sinistcha can buy turns with Rage Powder, Protect, and Strength Sap, but it is vulnerable to concentrated physical pressure and burn. Farigiraf’s Helping Hand and Trick Room support are valuable only if it can survive the opening assault.

reflections.summary: Your game plan of applying immediate pressure while denying Trick Room paid off early when Farigiraf fainted turn 2. A key sequence of double protect reads from the opponent around the Sinistcha switch-in stalled your momentum and cost you Incineroar. A critical Thunderbolt onto Metagross on turn 10 turned a likely 2v1 endgame into a 1v1, but Rotom-Wash had such a commanding special-defensive advantage over the heavily debuffed Archaludon that the endgame was unwinnable for the opponent. You won the series because your team-preview brought the correct disruption and priority, and your late-game positioning on Rotom-Wash was decisive.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent, continue bringing Incineroar, Metagross, Dragapult, and Rotom-Wash. Your disruptive core punishes their reliance on Farigiraf and Sinistcha for setup. Consider respecting the double Protect pattern more aggressively by predicting and using setup turns yourself. In future series, you could explore bringing Klefki over Dragapult for Prankster Thunder Wave to further disrupt Trick Room, but Dragapult’s offensive pressure and Will-O-Wisp were effective. Clawitzer remains a poor fit into Archaludon. Your registered six was well-suited; no major roster change is required.
reflections.notebook: Opponent relies heavily on Farigiraf for Trick Room setup; it will often Protect turn 1. They will eagerly double Protect to reposition after a faint. Sinistcha is used to absorb hits and heal with Strength Sap, but can be overwhelmed with consistent pressure. Archaludon is their main special attacker and can be crippled by multiple Draco Meteor SpA drops. Mamoswine is a physical threat with Life Orb and priority Ice Shard, but frail. In a rematch, target Farigiraf early to prevent Trick Room, and preserve Incineroar’s Intimidate and Fake Out to disrupt their pivots. Rotom-Wash is a safe late-game win condition once Archaludon’s SpA is lowered.
